To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections are huge for hard exclusive meson electroproduction at small xB, but that they can be substantially reduced by the use of an improved factorization formula, and that the NLO corrections to the target polarization asymmetry are small for ρ electroproduction, and large for ω electroproduction, at large xB.

(a) the size of next-leading order corrections is huge at small x, (b) they are substantial in typical fixed target kinematics, (c) they are small in the transversely polarized target asymmetry at small x, and (d) they are large in the same asymmetry at large x.

1) the next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections in the hard exclusive meson-production cross sections at small xB are huge; 2) the NLO corrections to the cross section in the typical fixed target kinematics are substantial; and 3) the NLO effects in the target asymmetry are very small for ϕ meson production but can be substantial in the case of ω.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hard exclusive meson electroproduction in the kinematic region of small Bjorken x and large photon virtualities.
the study of exclusive meson production processes in the framework of the collinear factorizaton approach, with the aim of providing a consistent theoretical description of these processes.
the study of the QCD structure of the nucleon and the dynamics of the strong interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
radiative corrections to exclusive meson production are large and must be taken into account.

the collinear approach is not reliable in the kinematics of fixed-target experiments, but that the next-to-leading order calculation is indispensable in order to understand the physics of exclusive meson production in the kinematics accessible at HERA.
radiative corrections are very large and should not be ignored in the interpretation of data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
radiative corrections are very important and must be taken into account in any quantitative analysis of hard exclusive meson electroproduction.

radiative corrections to the cross section and to the transverse target spin asymmetry can be large in hard exclusive meson electroproduction, and that their size depends strongly on the model for the nucleon distribution functions.
radiative corrections are important in the kinematic range of the HERA experiments and should be taken into account in the extraction of parton distribution functions from the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the kinematic region of interest, radiative corrections are not under control and the theoretical description of exclusive meson production is still incomplete.
the next-to-leading order effects should be taken into account when comparing experimental results with theoretical models, especially in the case of ω photoproduction.
the next-to-leading order contributions to hard exclusive mesons production are large and cannot be neglected.
